suggestions.reason: None of the four expectations check whether the deliverable workflow JSON actually complies with the platform's own task-ID format rule ([0-9a-f]{1,4}, documented at SKILL.md lines 352, 508, 1264, 1325 and AGENTS.md rule 9). The produced artifact (outputs/foreach-device-loop-example.json) uses three non-hex task IDs -- g6h7, h7i8, j8k9 -- which contain the letters g/h/i/j/k that fall outside [0-9a-f]. This directly contradicts the transcript's own claim (line 31) that the JSON was built 'following Guide 1's mapping rules (task ID format [0-9a-f]{1,4}...)' and that it was 'validated'. Per the skill's own documentation this would cause project-import rejection and silent $var resolution failures if ever imported. A stronger eval would assert that every task ID in the produced example matches ^[0-9a-f]{1,4}$ (excluding workflow_start/workflow_end), since this is an easy, deterministic, and currently-failing check that the four existing assertions do not cover.

eval_feedback.overall: The four core expectations are well-designed and discriminating -- they require the agent to correctly cite specific, verifiable skill constraints and to actually apply them correctly in a working example, and this run genuinely did both, cross-referencing a live production asset export as independent confirmation. However, none of the assertions catch a real defect I found in the delivered artifact: three task IDs (g6h7, h7i8, j8k9) violate the skill's hard hex-only task ID rule ([0-9a-f]{1,4}), directly contradicting the transcript's explicit claim of compliance and 'validation'. Recommend adding a task-ID-format assertion to this eval family so this class of defect is caught automatically.

expectations.text: States loop body tasks must not transition to error handlers outside the loop

The final answer section restates this explicitly: 'loop body tasks should never transition out to an external error handler -- let the forEach task's own state: error transition be the loop's single exit point for errors.'
